title: Lunar127 17T@1M MVP
primaryHypothesis: The carrier-anchored virtual console can sustain at least 1,000,000 sequential hologram epochs per second while a deterministic compute envelope of exactly 17,000,000 FLOP-equivalent operations per epoch remains selectively reconstructable and reference-verifiable.

program.name: VCK-2 17T@1M deterministic virtual vector program
program.semantics: Each lane evaluates one deterministic virtual FP32 multiply then add (two FLOP-equivalent operations). Full 4096-lane commands cover 8,499,200 lanes and one 800-lane tail covers the final 800 lanes.
program.floatSemantics: FP32 after input conversion, FP32 after multiply, FP32 after add; outputs serialized IEEE-754 little-endian float32.
program.availabilityBoundary: The 17 TFLOP/s-eq figure is represented deterministic compute availability at a 1 MHz epoch rate. It is not conventional measured hardware TFLOPS unless every represented operation is physically executed in real time.

passCriteria: Carrier SHA-256 matches the fixed Lunar127 page anchor.
Measured sequential AVK-1 transition rate is at least 1,000,000 epochs/s.
AVK-1 chain state at epoch 1,000,000 matches the predetermined reference.
The VCK-2 program defines exactly 17,000,000 FLOP-equivalent operations per epoch.
All predetermined selective compute-range SHA-256 challenges match.
The complete 8,500,000-lane compute output at epoch 1,000,000 matches its predetermined SHA-256.
The complete 262,144-byte hologram state at epoch 1,000,000 matches its predetermined SHA-256.
measurementBoundary: PASS demonstrates the defined virtual/reconstructable compute-availability model. 17 TFLOP/s-eq is not a claim of 17 trillion physically executed floating-point operations per second on the host.
